properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): #631's check holds each derived declaration only to what the declaration itself names — the functions it lists (one call deep, `self.` calls only, no const tables), the edges it lists, and its own components list. No check starts from an independent population: the crate's code, or the rule's own composition. So an undeclared deeper read, an undeclared relation and padded components were all invisible, and 13 declarations were padded to pass the intersection check
properties.source: R-J2 (dev_reflow2 hub fix agent), a Rust transitive scanner run inside crates/reflow2-core/tests/derived_relations_are_declared_and_checked.rs against origin/main 87f17ec (after #631, squash 6329079); graph-primitives fact:monitoring-pass-3-reflow2-pr-631-2026-09-29 and fact:reflow2-derived-declarations-diff-against-the-study-2026-09-29
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-29, on graph-primitives' monitoring pass 3 of reflow2 #631, under Anthony's "Fix all the root causes".

① OBSERVED (monitor, Python replica of the scanner): (a) readiness_gate reads HAS_READINESS two calls deep (readiness_report → resolve_gate → best_measured_level), the declaration omits it, the test passes; (b) a NEW derived relation nobody declared fails nothing; (c) a function that merely names the right edges passes; (d) 14 of 23 declarations list components that differ from their composition, 13 padded to match the edges read. Expected: the accepted requirement's "a check fails when the code derives a relation nothing declares". NOT affected: the declared-to-code direction for directly-read edges, which works.

② PRECEDENT: searched child-reflow2 and graph-primitives on the raw words; only the monitor's two facts. Class-level precedent: chg:bl159-gate-list-cross-check (two hand-kept records checked one way) and the skill_lint "checks names only" root cause.

③ CANDIDATES from the bones (Intent: requirement states the right thing, accepted; Assurance: the test ran green in CI and its own net pins blanking only; Implementation: the scanner): C1 depth-1 call following; C2 only `self.` calls followed; C3 src/ subdirectories unscanned; C4 edges named through const tables unseen; C5 the check's populations are drawn from the declaration file itself; C6 the observation is wrong (a Python copy).

④⑤ MEASURED, in Rust, by a transitive walk (all call forms, writers excluded, const/static tables followed) over the crate at 87f17ec:
- readiness_gate: HAS_READINESS two deep — CONFIRMED. Its HAS_TEMPORAL_FACT/VALID_FROM were satisfied by forecast_readiness, which takes &mut self (a writer); the gate's own reads of them are also two deep (earliest_clearing_forecast).
- impact: propagate_from → impact_neighbors reads BLOCKS, CONTRADICTS, MASKS, RISKS, VIOLATES through the RISK_EDGES const, declared nowhere. ONE call deep: the old scanner missed it because it cannot see a const, and so did the monitor's replica (C6 partly true: the replica shared the blind spot).
- budget_rollup reaches discontinued (scan_live_nodes → discontinued_ids); arrival_delta reaches delivered AND checked; neither `over` names them.
- C3 refuted as a live cause: 0 edge references under foundation/ or graphalg/.
- 179 functions name an edge type; 135 are answered for by no declaration, and nothing lists them.
- (d) reproduced exactly: 14 of 23 components differ from the composition's primitives, 13 with extras. Edge readings: 17 composites, 0 differ. Removing the padding makes 10 declared edges share no primitive with the rule (level_mismatch DEPENDS_ON, budget_rollup DEPENDS_ON/PROVIDES/CONSUMES, readiness_gate HAS_TEMPORAL_FACT/VALID_FROM, flow_step_order TRIGGERS, assigned_decision AUTHORED_BY, arrival_delta HAS_SNAPSHOT) — so the padding stood in for compositions that do not state what the rule reads.

⑥ CLASS: C1, C2 and C4 are triggers. The cause is C5: every check in the file is anchored on the declarations — the functions they name, the edges they list, the components they list — so it can only find disagreement INSIDE what was declared, and a declaration can be shaped to pass it. Would the class fix have stopped the others? Yes: a walk of everything the code reaches finds HAS_READINESS, RISK_EDGES and the missing `over`; a population drawn from the crate catches a new relation; holding components to the composition removes the padding.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a function computes a derived relation is a judgement about meaning, not mechanically decidable; what is mechanical is the population of edge-reading functions, which can be ratcheted. (c) needs rules a machine evaluates, the planned rule engine. Call resolution is by name and over-approximates.

CLOSED 2026-09-29: fixed by reflow2 PR #633 (squash 26b1ed2); its change record is in main's committed export, not this live store. Verified read-only on origin/main: derived_relations_are_declared_and_checked.rs walks transitively from every declared function (all call forms, any depth, const tables, never into a writer); every_function_that_names_an_edge_is_declared_or_listed draws its population from the crate against schema/derived/edge_readers.yaml; every_components_list_is_the_primitives_its_composition_writes holds components to Reading::composition_primitives; relations.yaml now lists readiness_gate's HAS_READINESS and impact's risk edges. The 132 `unjudged` entries in edge_readers.yaml sit under a count that may only shrink: that ratchet is the mechanical form ⑨ named, not this cause. Checking the RULE against the code still needs the planned rule engine (⑨).
